title: Synevid lineage comparison envelope (Pillar 1)
description: The output document of `autopsy lineage`: the identity transitions between two revisions as `autopsy-temporal::detect_lineage` asserts them, plus the revision accounting and the CLI's caveats. Closed: every field the command can emit is declared and nothing else validates. The load-bearing property is that `coverage` is `verified` only when the file enumeration was complete AND every event was proven by a byte-identical content digest; a skipped blob or a truncated file list makes the event set a stated *lower bound* (`partial`), and two empty revisions are `unsupported` rather than an empty pass. Only a confident rename or move preserves identity; a similarity-based match never does.

from.description: The earlier revision. Its `resolved` is `null` only in the one synthesized case: `to` is a root commit, so the comparison is against the empty tree.

events.description: The identity transitions, in the engine's canonical order (`from`, then `to`, then kind, with `null` sorting first). Empty is a statement — no path identity changed — and is not the same statement as "there was nothing to compare", which is `coverage: unsupported`.

coverage.description: `verified` only when both revisions were enumerated completely and every event is confident. `partial` when any event is not confident, any entry was skipped (gitlink or over the byte bound), or the file list hit its bound — in each of those cases the event set is a lower bound, and the `notes` say which bound was hit and with what counts. `unsupported` when both revisions contain no files: there is no identity transition to report, which is not the same answer as "none happened". `unknown` is never emitted here: a revision that cannot be read is an analysis error, not a silence.

notes.description: The CLI's own statements about the document, in prose — always including the engine's similarity caveat (a token signature, not a parse: only byte-identical content with a unique counterpart reaches `verified`), plus any skip, truncation or root-commit accounting that applies.

revision.description: The expression the user wrote, or the derived one for a defaulted argument (`HEAD~1 (first parent)`, or the empty-tree notice for a root `to`).

resolved.description: The commit id the expression resolved to. `null` only for the synthesized empty revision.

files.description: Files that reached the engine — not files present in the tree, unless the two skip counters and `truncated` are all zero.

gitlinks_skipped.description: Submodule entries (mode 160000): their contents live in another repository, so they can be neither compared nor reported.

truncated.description: True when the file list stopped at the bound. A skipped path could have been a rename, which is why any of these three conditions forces `partial`.

kind.description: The engine's `LineageEventKind` vocabulary, exhaustively: a schema that rejects the engine's own output is worse than no schema, and a variant this enum misses would be exactly that.

from.description: Canonical path before the transition; `null` for additions.

to.description: Canonical path after the transition; `null` for removals.

similarity.description: `1.0` exactly when content digests are equal; otherwise the token-signature score. A score never makes an event `verified`.

coverage.description: Narrower than the document-level states on purpose: the engine emits `verified` (byte-identical, unique counterpart) or `partial` (similarity or ambiguity). `unsupported` and `unknown` cannot occur on an event, and saying so in the schema is what makes a future occurrence a schema failure instead of a silent one.

ambiguity.description: Present exactly when `coverage` is not `verified`: the engine's contract, asserted in both directions by the conformance test.

candidates.description: Sorted candidate counterparts, excluding the chosen one when one exists. Legitimately empty when the best match beat the runner-up by the required margin — the `reason` still says why the match could not verify.

identity_preserved.description: Confident renames and moves: the only events that assert identity survives. Zero is the correct answer on an ambiguous history, not a failure.
